title: (No AI) NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy
content:
![](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/268844_NY_Times_Cooking_App_JTuohy_0006.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

The NYT Cooking app now has a built in AI assistant. | Photo: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy / The Verge

Around 7PM each weeknight, I find myself standing in front of the fridge, trying to decide on something for dinner that won't make my husband complain, "Chicken _again_?" Yes, I should meal plan more, but I don't, so this is where I'm at. A nightly battle in which the chicken usually wins.

Recently, my best weapon in this fight has been AI. Between [Alexa Plus in the Echo smart display](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1007565/amazon-alexa-plus-review-one-year-echo-show-dot-max#:~:text=I%20recently%20snapped,experience%20I%E2%80%99ve%20tested.) on my kitchen counter, the [Samsung Food app](https://www.theverge.com/2024/8/31/24231740/samsung-food-plus-vision-ai-food-list-management-ifa-2024) on my fridge, and even an [AI-powered cooking robot](https://www.theverge.com/tech/840599/posha-robot-chef-review), AI has become my go-to sous chef - albeit one I need to keep a close eye on. It's helped me swap ingredients, generate ideas, fix things when I mess up, and yes, even …

[Read the full story at The Verge.](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1029489/nyt-cooking-ai-assistant-review)

title: (No AI) The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
author: Terrence O’Brien
content:
![An image of Nvidia’s logo](https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2025/06/STK083_NVIDIA_2.jpg?quality=90&strip=all&crop=0,0,100,100)

Concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia are doing their due diligence when it comes to vetting Chinese firms cleared to handle the company's H200 AI chips. According to _[The New York Times](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/07/business/economy/nvidia-chips-chinese-firms.html)_, New Matrix is on the list of approved firms, yet its offices are empty, "a hollow gray shell with wires dangling from the ceiling where lights should be." In fact, the paper could find little evidence that the company exists in any meaningful way:

> Only scant information can be found online about New Matrix, which was created 17 months ago. At the building that New Matrix lists as its address, a company directory does not …
